body: Overall I like the change (fit by default). What I dislike: - Now there's no way to reset to `1.0` zoom. - `Zoom Reset` button still uses the same icon showing `1`, which suggests it will reset to `1.0` zoom. That's misleading. --- I think maybe we could go with something similar to e.g. 2D view in the editor: - `-`, `+` buttons as currently, with zoom percentage shown between, clicking which resets to `100%`. - Additional button (not sure if on the left/right) for "zoom to fit". Possibly the same icon as for distraction free mode? - Keep it zooming in by default like currently in this PR.

I'm working on this. For now I've updated the icon and tooltip for the former reset button. I will add the zoom level display when I can. 

I have also changed the fitting behavior to take into account the size of the frames on the screen not just the size of the texture. My intent behind this change is to make the new button have a use when working with large textures. The initial implementation would have it behave exactly like the reset button for big textures. I thought to have it zoom out to fit large textures and, while that at first seemed more consistent, it's not helpful if the ratio of texture size to frame sizes is large. I see the purpose in adding this fitting behavior in the first place to be making frames easier to click. In this way this new change to the behavior is consistent.

To summarize the new overall functionality of this button:
1. Zoom in if the texture is too small to make the frames bigger
1. Zoom in if frames are too small to make the frames bigger
1. Zoom out if frames are too big respectively to show more frames.

I have additionally made the zoom update when changing the size of frames if the zoom has been fitted. Any feedback would be greatly appreciated but I would especially appreciate feedback on this aspect.
I believe I have implemented the recommended changes
@kleonc I'm wondering what your feedback on the changes I've made are

@WesleyClements Firstly: sorry for no earlier review/response! > I have also changed the fitting behavior to take into account the size of the frames on the screen not just the size of the texture. My intent behind this change is to make the new button have a use when working with large textures. The initial implementation would have it behave exactly like the reset button for big textures. I thought to have it zoom out to fit large textures and, while that at first seemed more consistent, it's not helpful if the ratio of texture size to frame sizes is large. I see the purpose in adding this fitting behavior in the first place to be making frames easier to click. In this way this new change to the behavior is consistent. Just tested it with [a big texture](https://engvee.itch.io/animated-isometric-prototyping-hero), and AFAICT the button makes an impression like it's not working: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/816d05fd-d545-454b-b27a-d02ff44d663c I do think it would indeed make more sense if it would open zoomed out to show the whole texture: Currently after opening|Suggested
(something alike) -|- | IMO, at least that would be the expected behavior based on the current button icon. The current icon+behavior would make me think it's broken (if I was not aware of this PR). So if we'd want something different than just "fit the whole texture into the view", then it would probably need a different icon (no idea what would be intuitive). This makes me wonder whether we maybe want 2 new buttons there: - "Fit texture to view" which would make the whole texture be shown. - The second one zooming so a single frame is somehow nicely shown. > I have additionally made the zoom update when changing the size of frames if the zoom has been fitted. Any feedback would be greatly appreciated but I would especially appreciate feedback on this aspect. I dislike this. I think the "fitting" should be a one-time action, on button press (+the automatic one when opening the dialog in case we're not restoring some previously set settings for the given texture). I find it surprising for the zoom to auto-adjust when changing frame settings. No idea if it's just me but this might be against the principle of least astonishment. However, if it will be decided that active auto-fitting is desired, then the button enabling it should be a toggle (so the user could see if it's active or not based on the button state). --- Note that (from [`4.6.dev5` blog post](https://godotengine.org/article/dev-snapshot-godot-4-6-dev-5/)): > Dev 5 is jam-packed with new features and enhancements as contributors try to finish off their big contributions before we hit the feature freeze and Beta 1 shortly after. As a reminder, feature freeze is the period where we stop merging anything except for bug fixes as we shift our focus to polishing the existing code in preparation for release. **We plan on entering our feature freeze on December 3** and only releasing one more dev snapshot before entering the Beta phase. So if we want any improvements here be merged into `4.6` we need to make this happen by tomorrow, December 3 (again, my bad on not reviewing this earlier). What I consider as mergeable (I can approve right away and mark it for the production team for merging): - Changing zoom buttons from to , as is. - Auto zooming in when opening the dialog with a new texture (can be as is, i.e. not zooming out big textures - still an improvement). Also fine for me to approve right now (but not necessary): - Adding new "Fit texture to view" which would make the whole texture be shown (with the currently used icon (the "distraction free mode" one)). Regarding the added "Fit to frames" button / its behavior, and the automatic zoom changes on changing frame settings, I'm not sure about them (the expected behavior / whether it's needed). Hence I suggest removing them from this PR, and if desired open a separate follow-up PR for that (and possibly make it be more discussed (in a proposal?), not just between you and me, to get some more opinions). In case you do want the mergeable part I've mentioned above be merged to `4.6` but you're not able to apply the changes by tomorrow please let me know, in such case I could open a PR extracting those myself (and co-author you of course). But in case you do not hurry for `4.6` then it's of course fine to not split this PR anyhow.

@kleonc No worries about the delay! I could have pinged you sooner. I really appreciate the feedback!

I've removed all the experimentation and these should be the requested changes.

@kleonc Last bit cleaned up and also caught the potential for the zoom fit value to fall outside of the min and max zoom values which would cause snapping when trying to use the `+` and `-` buttons on extremely large textures. I don't know if this is necessary but it makes the implementation consistent with the previous design.
Good catch! Agree that clamping to ensure min-max range is a good change. 👍
